message.content: Copernicus crafted his heliocentric theory during Europe's transformative Renaissance and Reformation era. The Protestant movement was fracturing the Church's political grip, while the Ottoman Empire pressed into Central Europe. The printing press was spreading radical ideas faster than any institution could suppress them. No cactiform structure in nature, however, mirrors the upheaval his solar model would ignite in science and governance. Nation-states consolidated power, and the papacy still held supreme jurisdiction over natural philosophy. It was a climate where challenging geocentrism risked ecclesiastical censure, yet intellectual curiosity surged forward.
